A wind or irradiance simulation report, an annex to the loan agreement, or an internal plan — say which. Three years on, when the figure is challenged, this is the only thing that can answer where it came from.
Energy is not a single number but a distribution: a windier\n year than the last gives different energy, and nobody controls that.

P50 is the expectation, used for planning. P90 is the level a bank uses to assess debt service. Declare one level and call it "the plan" and every question about energy risk loses its place to be answered.

It must hold that P50 ≥ P75 ≥ P90. The declared figures are %(ds)s.\n\nP90 is the level exceeded in 90%% of years, so it is the LOWEST figure — a bank uses exactly that level because it needs near certainty. Declared the other way round, every subsequent risk analysis is inverted while still running perfectly smoothly.

P50 ≥ P75 ≥ P90. The more certain it is to be achieved, the lower the figure — P90 is the level exceeded in 90% of years, and it is the level a bank uses to assess debt service. Declared the other way round, every subsequent risk analysis is inverted while still running perfectly smoothly, so the system blocks it at save time.
